text.p: More than 700,000 Prudential Insurance Co of America policyholders have expressed interest in receiving restitution for deceptive sales practices, a source familiar with the situation said.
Policyholders have until June 1 to notify Prudential they want to participate in the restitution process, but there is a 10-day grace period beyond that.
However, this is just a first step in the process and the number of policyholders who actually complete claim forms and qualify for restitution may end up to be much lower, Prudential said.
But assuming that 700,000 policyholders complete the claim forms and qualify for restitution, the cost to Prudential could top $1.6 billion, assuming an average restitution cost of $2,300.
That tops earlier estimates of the potential cost of the class-action settlement to Prudential.
The restitution process was set up as part of a settlement of allegations that Prudential sales agents misled policyholders about what they were purchasing.

As part of a class-action settlement approved in March, Prudential agreed to pay at least $410 million to people who purchased as many as 10.7 million permanent life insurance policies between 1982 and 1995.
But the settlement had been expected to cost Prudential at least $1.2 billion and have a total value to policyholders of nearly $2 billion.

After Prudential receives these initial responses from policyholders, the company has 75 days to send them claim forms, asking them for detailed information about how they were misled by Prudential sales agents.
Policyholders have 90 days to return these claims forms to Prudential and the claims then will be evaluated, Prudential said.
Prudential said it has not received 700,000 responses, but declined to give further details.
It said it would release participation figures after the claims paying period, which could take at least a year.
But a spokesman for the company said, "we believe we've taken extraordinary steps to get people to respond."
Melvyn Weiss, a lawyer heading the class-action team, also declined to specify the number of responses received.
But he said the response has been "far in excess" of expectations.
